title: Kubernetes Basics
description: An introduction to Kubernetes covering its architecture, core API objects, networking model, and common operational workflows. By the end of this plan you will be able to deploy a containerised application, expose it via a Service, and troubleshoot common cluster issues.

modules.title: Cluster Architecture
modules.description: How a Kubernetes cluster is structured: the control plane components that manage state and the worker nodes that run workloads.

lessons.title: The Control Plane
lessons.description: The set of components that make global decisions about the cluster (scheduling, detecting and responding to cluster events).

concepts.title: kube-apiserver
concepts.description: The front-end for the Kubernetes control plane. It exposes the Kubernetes API, validates and processes REST requests, and is the only component that reads from and writes to etcd.

concepts.title: etcd
concepts.description: A consistent and highly-available key-value store used as Kubernetes' backing store for all cluster data. All cluster state and configuration live here.

concepts.title: kube-scheduler
concepts.description: Watches for newly created Pods that have no assigned node and selects a node for them to run on based on resource requirements, affinity rules, and other constraints.

concepts.title: kube-controller-manager
concepts.description: Runs built-in controller loops (e.g. ReplicaSet controller, Node controller, Job controller). Each controller watches the current state of the cluster and drives it towards the desired state.

lessons.title: Worker Nodes
lessons.description: The machines (physical or virtual) that run containerised workloads. Each node runs two mandatory components.

concepts.title: kubelet
concepts.description: An agent that runs on every node. It ensures containers described in PodSpecs are running and healthy, communicating with the kube-apiserver to receive work and report status.

concepts.title: kube-proxy
concepts.description: Maintains network rules on nodes. These rules allow network communication to Pods from inside or outside the cluster. kube-proxy uses the OS packet filtering layer (e.g. iptables or IPVS).

modules.title: Core Workload Objects
modules.description: The fundamental Kubernetes objects used to define and manage containerised workloads.

lessons.title: Pods
lessons.description: The smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes. A Pod wraps one or more containers that share network and storage.

concepts.title: Pod definition
concepts.description: A Pod spec declares the desired containers, their images, exposed ports, environment variables, volume mounts, and resource requests/limits.

concepts.title: Pod lifecycle
concepts.description: The stages a Pod moves through: Pending → Running → Succeeded / Failed / Unknown. Understanding lifecycle is essential for troubleshooting stuck or crashing Pods.

lessons.title: Deployments
lessons.description: A higher-level object that manages a ReplicaSet to ensure a specified number of Pod replicas are running. Deployments support rolling updates and rollbacks.

concepts.title: Deployment spec
concepts.description: Defines the desired state: number of replicas, Pod template, and update strategy (RollingUpdate or Recreate).

concepts.title: Rolling updates and rollbacks
concepts.description: A rolling update replaces Pods incrementally so the application stays available. If a rollout fails, kubectl rollout undo reverses to the previous revision.

modules.title: Networking and Service Discovery
modules.description: How Pods communicate with each other and how external clients reach workloads inside the cluster.

lessons.title: Services
lessons.description: An abstract way to expose an application running as a set of Pods. Services provide a stable IP and DNS name that load-balances across healthy Pod replicas.

concepts.title: ClusterIP Service
concepts.description: The default Service type. Exposes the Service on a cluster-internal IP, reachable only from within the cluster.

concepts.title: NodePort and LoadBalancer Services
concepts.description: NodePort exposes the Service on each node's IP at a static port. LoadBalancer provisions an external load balancer (cloud provider) and assigns a public IP.
